one_month_reasoning: No PANW earnings fall inside the window to 2026-11-05. Fiscal year ends July 31; Q1 FY27 (quarter ending Oct 31) has no announced date. Past Q1 reports came on 2024-11-20 and 2025-11-19, and the FY26 Q3/Q4 reports came about two weeks later than the year before (June 2, Sept 1), so the report most likely lands mid-to-late November or later, outside the window. In the window: peer and hyperscaler earnings season (read-through on security budgets and AI data-center firewall demand), macro data, and sentiment. The stock closed at $419.91, above its 52-week high of $409.50, roughly triple its 52-week low of $139.57 (Feb-2026, when the company itself bought back $1.0B of stock at $147.69). The Sept 14 13.6% one-day pop came from AI-risk headlines, not from fundamentals. Short-term reversal after a sharp breakout and positive momentum roughly offset each other, so I stay near neutral: median $418 (about flat) with lognormal sigma 13.4% (47% annual vol / 3.5). No catalyst-driven skew.

fair_value.method: Blend of 65% P/E (65x Oct-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of $5.22 = $340) and 35% DCF on owner FCF (adj. FCF less SBC; WACC 8.5%, g 4% = $217). Blended value is ~$297, about 29% below the $419.91 close. At 97x forward EPS against a 53x peer median, the stock prices growth well above management's own $20B FY30 NGS ARR path.

FY27 guide 29.5% + ~100bp leverage, consistent with CyberArk synergies running 3-6 months ahead of plan and 40% FY28 FCF margin target.
4.18 x 1.18 (revenue) x 30.5/29.5 (margin) / 1.015 (share-count creep, ESPP/SBC per S-8 and FY27 guide) = 5.02

Peer median fwd P/E 53.0x (12 peers, range 12.0x-259.8x); PANW today 97.1x. 65x = ~1.2x peer median, inside the range: premium limited because PANW's 3Y EPS CAGR forecast (14.4%) is below the peer median (16.1%), offset by scale, ~80% recurring revenue and 38-40% adj. FCF margins.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY27 revenue $14.15B, owner FCF margin 24% rising to 31% (adj. FCF 38-40% less SBC ~14% falling), growth 18% fading to 5% over 9 years, WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 4%, net cash ~$9.5B at Oct-2027, 860M shares; valued at Oct-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27: 38% adj FCF - ~14% SBC (Q4 FY26 SBC $487M x4 / $14.15B = 13.8%); FY28: 40% target - ~13% SBC; SBC ratio drifts down ~1pt/yr.
Starts from FY28 +18% (see P/E method), fades as NGS ARR approaches the $20B FY30 target and the base matures.

Judgment: 5Y beta 0.94 (cited) implies roughly market-level equity risk, so a large-cap market-like cost of capital of 8.5-9% is used, at the lower end given the net-cash balance sheet and ~80% recurring revenue. Sensitivity: WACC 8.0%-9.0% gives $196-$244/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Sum of reported balance-sheet items at 2026-07-31; plus ~$3.4B FY27 owner FCF retained by Oct-2027 (estimate).
FY27 guide 844-847M diluted, plus ~1.5% creep; 818M basic outstanding at 2026-08-31 per 10-K.

bear.story: The AI-security re-rating unwinds and PANW compresses toward the peer median: about 48x NTM EPS of ~$5.2. Possible triggers: organic NGS ARR growth fading below ~20% once CyberArk laps in Feb-2027 (reported revenue growth drops from 33-34% to ~20%), memory/storage cost pressure on hardware, a shortfall in the one-off LLM migration to Chronosphere that management already flagged would be smaller after Q1 FY27, or a broad high-multiple software sell-off.

base.story: PANW executes to guidance with modest beats, as it has every quarter in FY26 (Q4 revenue $3.41B vs $3.345-3.355B guide). NTM EPS ~$5.2 by Oct-2027. The multiple drifts down from 97x to ~73x as reported growth normalises post-CyberArk, but stays well above peers on scale, FCF margin and AI-security positioning.

bull.story: AI-driven security demand (agentic traffic up 9x in nine months, record firewall bookings for AI data centers) keeps NGS ARR well ahead of the $20B FY30 path. FY28 guidance in Aug/Sep 2027 implies ~20%+ organic growth and the 40% FCF margin. The sector keeps CRWD/NET-like multiples and PANW holds ~100x NTM EPS of ~$5.4.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 12.0x (CHKP) to 259.8x (RBRK) across 12 peers. EV/EBITDA 13.2x (CHKP) to 2,638x (CRWD) for the 9 peers with data (NET, S, RBRK n/a). Basis, applied identically to all peers and PANW: forward P/E = price / NTM consensus EPS (adjusted, as published by StockAnalysis); EV/EBITDA = trailing (TTM) GAAP EBITDA, since a consistent forward EBITDA was not available. Because GAAP EBITDA is depressed by SBC and acquisition amortisation, EV/EBITDA is shown for reference only and is not used in valuation. The ev_ebitda_fwd field therefore holds TTM values. Growth column = consensus 3-year EPS CAGR (revenue CAGR for RBRK).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: PANW trades at 97.1x forward P/E and 219.9x TTM EV/EBITDA, against peer medians of 53.0x and 83.2x. That is above the median but inside the range: below CRWD (198x), NET (240x) and RBRK (260x); above DDOG (105x is close), FTNT (52x), ZS (43x), OKTA (54x). I apply 65x to Oct-2027 NTM EPS, about 1.2x the peer median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only a limited premium is justified. For it: scale (FY26 revenue $11.48B, FY27 guide $14.1-14.2B), about 80% subscription and support revenue (10-K), 38.4% adjusted FCF margin in FY26 with a 40% FY28 target, organic NGS ARR +28% (Q3 FY26 call), and platformized-cohort NRR above 120%. These are structural and should persist through the horizon. Against a larger premium: PANW's consensus 3Y EPS CAGR (14.4%) is below the peer median (16.1%) and FY27 EPS growth is only ~9% because of CyberArk share issuance (112M shares, 10-Q) and SBC (~14% of revenue). So the 97x market multiple is not justified on fundamentals versus peers. I cap the premium at ~20% over the median (65x). The very high CRWD/NET/RBRK multiples reflect a sector-wide AI-security re-rating that I do not treat as a durable anchor.

thesis_break_reason: $250 is ~48x Oct-2027 NTM EPS, below the 53x peer median, and ~40% under the current price, larger than a one-sigma annual move. If PANW trades there it would most likely mean the fundamentals cracked, not just that the multiple cooled. Examples: NGS ARR guidance cut or organic ARR growth falling toward the teens, CyberArk/Idira growth slipping from the ~21% reported, hardware margins squeezed by memory costs, or the FY28 40% FCF margin target withdrawn. Above that level, moves are consistent with ordinary de-rating of a 97x stock.

Annual meeting (2025 say-on-pay was rejected) and expiry of the remaining $1.0B buyback authorisation on 2026-12-31; renewal or lapse
Q2 FY27 results; CyberArk (closed 2026-02-11) laps, so reported growth falls from 33-34% toward organic ~20%
Q3 FY27 results; first year of new segment reporting (Network Security, Cortex, Identity) gives organic visibility
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 guidance; check against 40% FY28 adj. FCF margin target and $20B FY30 NGS ARR path
Memory/storage component cost inflation in hardware (~10% of revenue); AI-security sentiment swings (e.g. Sept 14 pop on AI-risk headlines)

key_uncertainties: Durability of the sector-wide AI-security re-rating: the stock is up 95% in a year while FY27 EPS is guided up only ~9%; it trades at 97x forward EPS, and peers CRWD/NET at ~200x+.
Organic growth after CyberArk laps in Feb-2027: the FY27 revenue guide of +23-24% includes ~6 months of inorganic contribution.
Size and persistence of the large-LLM-customer migration to Chronosphere, which gave a nine-figure Q4 ARR benefit that management says will be smaller and last through Q1 FY27.
Hardware memory cost inflation versus record firewall demand from AI data centers.
SBC (~14% of revenue) and share creep diluting non-GAAP EPS growth to ~9% in FY27.
Governance: say-on-pay was rejected in Dec-2025; a new executive change-in-control policy was adopted Aug-2026.
reasoning: Primary-document read. FY26 (FYE July 31) revenue was $11.48B (+25%), Q4 revenue $3.41B (+34%), NGS ARR $9.10B (+63%), RPO $21.2B, non-GAAP EPS $3.84, adj. FCF margin 38.4%. The headline growth is inflated by CyberArk (closed 2026-02-11; 112M shares issued) and Chronosphere (closed 2026-01-29, $3.35B). The Q2 FY26 release (before CyberArk closed; Chronosphere only 2 days in) showed revenue +15% and NGS ARR +33%; the Q3 call put organic NGS ARR at +28% and organic RPO at +22%. FY27 guidance: revenue $14.10-14.20B (+23-24%), NGS ARR +22-23%, non-GAAP EPS $4.16-4.19 (only ~+9% because of dilution), op margin 29.5%, adj. FCF margin 38%, 844-847M shares. Management targets 40% FCF margin in FY28 and $20B NGS ARR in FY30. At $419.91 the stock is ~100x FY27 EPS and ~97x NTM consensus, against a 12-peer median of 53x. My EPS path (FY28 $5.02, FY29 $5.83; Oct-2027 NTM $5.22) at a justified 65x gives $340. A DCF on owner FCF (net of SBC) gives $217. Blended fair value is $297. For the 12-month distribution I don't put all the weight on fundamentals: the sector re-rating is strong and broad (CRWD 198x, NET 240x), consensus targets cluster at $396-410, and the stock has strong 12-month momentum (+95%). So my median is $380 (~-10%), between fair value and spot, with the scenario mix bear $250 (30%) / base $380 (45%) / bull $540 (25%), mean ~$381. The ladder is a lognormal around $380 with sigma 0.42, a bit below the 47% realized vol because realized includes the Feb crash and the rally, and a bit wider in the left tail. That gives P(>= today's $420) of about 40%. One month: no earnings in window, near-neutral. Limitations: the IR site (investors.paloaltonetworks.com) returned errors, so management statements were checked via full call transcripts; peer multiples come from one data provider on a single stated basis; consistent forward EBITDA was not available.
